text:
Miguel (CS): Customer acme-ai reporting sudden 503s for embed-heavy requests starting ~09:12 UTC, multiple regions. They pasted sample call and said it used to be fine.
Priya (SRE): Can you drop the request id + example payload? size of input, model, and whether it's streaming or batch?
Miguel (CS): request_id=rid_0b7f, payload ~1.2MB, embedding call, model=redwood-v2-embed-large, batch_size=8, toolcall=false, non-streaming. Happens on p95 latency and then 503s.
Sam (Support): I see matching 503s in gateway logs: "upstream: 502/503 after connect" around same time. Created support ticket #INC-12098 and alerted oncall.
CS Bot: @channel elevated to P1 — customer-facing outage impacting embeddings for 2 customers.
Priya (SRE): Looking at infra metrics — host pool node group gpu-a100-80 has GPU mem ballooning on node gpu-12. Kernel logs show repeated "CUDA OOM" followed by container SIGKILL and then later a SIGSEGV during hotprefetch.
Anya (Eng-runtime): paste from runner logs:
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:34Z] ERROR infer-runner[pid=8421]: CudaError: out of memory allocating 120M
[2026-03-18T09:12:34Z] ERROR infer-runner[pid=8421]: Attempting fallback quantized op
[2026-03-18T09:12:34Z] FATAL infer-runner[pid=8421]: signal SIGSEGV (Address not mapped to object)
#0  0x7ffdeadbeef in kv_prefetch::read_chunk()
#1  0x7ffabc1234 in runner::serve_batch()
```
Priya (SRE): That stack matches a prefetch path bug we've seen when memory pressure + large batch combines. Node restarted by kube because liveness probe failed.
Miguel (CS): Customer asking for repro steps — they want to know if billable tokens were charged during the failure window and if we can credit.
Sam (Support): Logged to billing team — asking for a partial credit while we investigate. Also asked the customer to hold traffic for now or reduce batch_size to 1 as a workaround.
Anya (Eng-runtime): Quick repro I ran locally with a trimmed payload: `python repro/embed_flood.py --model redwood-v2-embed-large --batch 8 --ctx 64k` reproduced OOM + segfault for me after ~20 iterations. Attaching small gdb bt: `#0 kv_prefetch::read_chunk(); #1 runner::serve_batch(); #2 start_thread`
Priya (SRE): Actions: 1) cordon pool gpu-a100-80 (done), 2) enable fallback to cpu-quantized-worker for routing (in progress), 3) collect core dump + nvcrash logs from gpu-12.
ops-bot: Core dump collected: s3://internal-dumps/6881234567/gpu-12-core.tgz (requires perms).
Anya (Eng-runtime): Repro notes: appears to be race between kv cache eviction and prefetch allocation when batch combines many long contexts. Proposed short-term patch: guard allocation with a soft memory check + immediate OOM fallback before touching pointer.
Priya (SRE): Can you make a hotfix PR and we can rollout to canary? Also need to confirm no auth/billing exploit — looks like normal authenticated traffic.
Anya (Eng-runtime): I'll open PR with test and small guard. Target canary in 15m.
Miguel (CS): Customer accepted temporary mitigation (reduce batch_size) and asked for ETA on fix and credits. I told them we have a patch going to canary and will follow up in 2 hours.
Sam (Support): Billing asked for affected req ids; Miguel attached `rid_0b7f` and a CSV of 18 request ids. Billing will compute credit.
Priya (SRE): Next steps: collect more heap profiles from canary after hotfix, roll to pool, uncordon nodes. If canary looks good, schedule full rollout and then close incident.
Miguel (CS): Adding postmortem checklist + owner assignment to INC-12098.
CS Bot: Incident INC-12098 updated: owner=Anya (Eng-runtime), severity=P1, sla-impact=high.
Sam (Support): Any blockers?
Anya (Eng-runtime): Need approvals for hotfix CI bypass for canary deploy (security signoff).
Priya (SRE): I have sec on call, will approve for canary only.
Miguel (CS): Thanks all — I'll keep CS updated and reply to customer now. :thumbsup:
Anya (Eng-runtime): PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/eng-runtime/pulls/5421 — includes guard + unit test. Can deploy to canary after approval.
Priya (SRE): Approving canary deploy now.
ops-bot: Canary deploy started at 09:37 UTC.
Anya (Eng-runtime): Canary looks stable after 25m under load test with large-batch embed script. No OOMs, no segfaults.
Priya (SRE): Uncordoned one node as experiment; will monitor p95 for 1h then rollout.
Miguel (CS): Customer acknowledged ETA and appreciated quick turnaround.
Sam (Support): Billing confirmed they'll propose a goodwill credit for the affected window.
CS Bot: Incident INC-12098 moved to monitoring (post-fix)."
